clue.text: See 9
Biblical woman from Messina omitted

indicators.note: from says the answer is a run of letters taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A woman of the Bible has been left out of something about the Sicilian city of Messina.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across the end of 'Messina' into the start of 'omitted'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament book of Ruth, Naomi is Ruth's mother-in-law.

clue.text: Seed in the air shot up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody
a nip is a small shot of spirits

explanation.surface: A seed blown into the air goes shooting upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TUNENIP round, so it reads PINENUT. 'shot' looks like a verb but here it is a noun: a nip of whisky. 'in the' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible kernel of a pine cone is a seed, eaten as a nut.

clue.text: Dog has a parting drink thus

indicators.note: parting says the words before it split the drink in two and sit in the gap

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a dog does, with the tongue
taken as written
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A dog splits a drink in two this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parting' looks like a goodbye, but here the words HAS A part the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lhasa apso is a small long-haired breed from Tibet.

clue.text: See 23
Giant turtle's head on bread

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of turtle

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A giant turtle's head is placed on top of some bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giant' looks like it describes the turtle, but it is the definition. 'on' is a link: in a down clue the T sits on top of ROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is a giant or ogre in Scandinavian folklore.

clue.text: Tower Bridge initially smothered in butter, half of tuna on top!

indicators.note: on top says this piece goes above the rest in a down answer
half of a four-letter word is its first two letters, here from tuna
smothered in says the letter is wrapped up inside the animal

parts.note: a butter is something that butts, such as a goat

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word Bridge

explanation.surface: Tower Bridge gets smeared in butter, with half a tuna on top, a strange recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower Bridge' reads as the London landmark, but 'Tower' alone is the definition: something that tows. 'butter' is the animal that butts, not the spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug pulls ships along, so it is a tower in the sense of one that tows.

clue.text: Shenanigans, fooling around with a holy person? That's not on!

indicators.note: fooling around says the letters are played about with and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the word on is removed from the pool, as That's not on says

explanation.surface: Someone plays pranks with a holy person, and is told that such behaviour is not acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange A HOLY PERSON with the O and N taken out ('That's not on!') and you get HORSEPLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean rowdy, mischievous fooling about.

clue.text: European outlaw stealing in, thus laid back

indicators.note: stealing means taking in, so the ban holds the reversed piece

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

indicators.note: laid back says these words are turned so that they read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A European criminal sneaks in, cool and relaxed about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid back' reverses IN + SO, giving OSNI, and 'stealing' puts that inside the outlaw word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bosnian comes from Bosnia, a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Jack cut through pegleg, or fixed the 23 problem?

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: through says the cut passes into the middle of the rearranged letters
fixed means put right, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged
a snip is a small cut

explanation.surface: Someone fixes a wooden leg and wonders whether that solved a problem from another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges PEGLEG OR into OGGERPLE, and 'through' runs the cut into it. '23' is the linked 23-across, RUNNING STITCH: here running gives the problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-distance runners often get sore nipples from their shirts rubbing, a well-known complaint.

clue.text: Rescuer swimming fast around eastern river

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap the other pieces
swimming suggests movement, so the letters of fast are mixed up

parts.note: the Tyne is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: A rescuer swims quickly around an eastern river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges FAST into SAFT, and 'around' wraps it round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety net catches people who fall, so it rescues them, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Party girl has to crash after 5.30?

indicators.note: after says the rest of the answer follows the opening piece

parts.note: 5.30 can be read as half five: half of the word five is its first two letters
Anna is a girl's name
to crash is to fail, as a computer does

explanation.surface: A girl at a party has to leave and sleep somewhere after half past five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like it describes the girl, but it is the definition. British speakers say 'half five' for 5.30.
explanation.definitionFit: Fianna Fáil is one of the main political parties in the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Redistribution of 1/10 for workers in the field?

indicators.note: redistribution means sharing out again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 1 is written ONE and 10 is the Roman numeral X

explanation.surface: A tenth of something is redistributed among farm workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Write 1 as ONE and 10 as the Roman X, then rearrange ONEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen are draught animals used to pull ploughs on a farm.

clue.text: Legally check sauce, opening at the back

indicators.note: the opening letter of the sauce is moved to the end

parts.note: pesto is a basil sauce

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether it is legal to put sauce on, with a gap left at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the P of PESTO from the front to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To estop is a legal term meaning to bar or preclude someone from asserting something.

clue.text: Queen admitting lines crossed over order for treasury

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the Queen holds the other pieces

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: over says the crossed lines come before the next piece

parts.note: two lines crossed make the letter X
a cheque is a written order to a bank to pay money

explanation.surface: A Queen lets in some crossed-out lines on an order for the treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: A crossed cheque, with two parallel lines drawn on it, is a real banking term, which helps the surface hide the X.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the British government's treasury department.

clue.text: Setter recalled club almost bandaging left arm

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the setter is the person who wrote the clue, so ME

indicators.note: bandaging means wrapping, so the shortened word goes around the letter
almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to club someone is to batter them

explanation.surface: A setter remembers a club nearly being used to bandage a left arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses ME to EM; 'almost' cuts the last letter, R, off BATTER. 'arm' looks like part of the injury, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To embattle is to prepare for war, which is to arm a force or fortify a place.

clue.text: Bronco just down the road, say, for pirate

indicators.note: say signals that the words sound like the answer when spoken

parts.note: a bronco is a bucker, a horse that bucks; something just down the road is near

explanation.surface: A wild horse lives just down the road from a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'bucker near' sounds like BUCCANEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer was a pirate in the Caribbean in the 17th century.

clue.text: Bitterness with which a friend welcomes single male

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the friend holds the other pieces

parts.note: a crony is a close friend
I is the Roman numeral for one, so single

explanation.surface: A friend gives a warm welcome to a single man, which causes bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with which' is just a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is bitter, angry feeling between people, usually in an argument.

clue.text: Trendy, like youth

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
to fancy something is to like it

explanation.surface: Being trendy is something enjoyed in youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is early childhood, the very start of a person's youth.

clue.text: Like a bird, perhaps, to be conceited

definitions.meaning: a cock is a male bird, so like a cock read jokily
too sure of yourself, arrogantly self-confident

explanation.surface: Being like a bird might mean being vain.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense makes the word an invented adjective from cock, a male bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocky describes someone who is boldly self-assured, like a strutting rooster.

clue.text: Kindness towards others — suspicious about it?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cautious word goes around it

parts.note: chary means wary or suspicious
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who is suspicious of kindness to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspicious' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity is generosity and goodwill shown to those in need.

clue.text: Four notes — though not picking them up?

parts.note: D is a musical note
E is a musical note
A is a musical note
F is a musical note

explanation.surface: Four notes are played, but someone does not hear them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' refers back to the notes: someone deaf cannot pick them up.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person cannot hear sounds such as notes.

clue.text: Old actress having tempestuous rage with Bogart

indicators.note: tempestuous means stormy, so the letters are thrown about and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A film star of the past flies into a stormy temper with Humphrey Bogart.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange RAGE + BOGART.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood star of the 1920s and 30s.

clue.text: Private part of going on a diet

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A private part of the body changes when someone goes on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Private part' together, but 'part of' is the indicator. The answer runs from 'goinG ON A Diet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gonad is a sex organ, so a private part of the body.

clue.text: Managing pain, needle required for it

parts.note: running a business means managing it
a stitch is a sharp pain in the side

explanation.surface: A manager in pain needs an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needle' looks medical, but it is a sewing needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A running stitch is a simple sewing stitch made with a needle.

clue.text: Minister did you say? Come again?

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister
is it? is a conversational reply like did you say?

explanation.surface: A minister asks a question, and someone asks him to repeat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come again?' reads as a request to repeat, but it is the definition: to visit once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit is to go back to a place, to come there again.

clue.text: Hard time with Inland Revenue turning over capital

indicators.note: turning over says the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a day is a period of time
IR is the abbreviation of Inland Revenue, the former UK tax office

explanation.surface: Someone has a hard time with the tax office, which turns over their capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' reverses HDAYIR. 'capital' looks like money, but it is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Worn out, ate, grabbing some sun

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so the meal word goes around it

parts.note: fed means ate, as in a baby has fed
a ray is a beam, some of the sun's light

explanation.surface: Someone tired out eats while catching a bit of sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ate' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Frayed means worn out at the edges, like old cloth.
